pr_title: Bluetooth: host: Add discovery of standard descriptor values
pr_body:
Add discovery of standard descriptor values. This provides a shorthand
instead of doing a read by UUID, allowing the application discovery
procedure to re-use the discover parameters for simple descriptors.

Fixes: #21489
pr_comments:
fixed compliance issues with spaces and parenthesis.
Rebased to include dependant PR for struct gatt_cpf definition.

issue_context.title: Allow to read any types during discovery
comments:
I have plans to make a pool of bt_att_req so we don't have to embedded them into the params, that would make them quite more slim, the other thing we have been planning is to support general discovery procedure, in that case you would just provide the service UUID you are interested in and it would do the discovery of all attributes within the service range when a general discovery is triggered.

I probably wouldn't go as far as to create a cache for the entire database since to make use of it in a generic form it would take a lot of memory to store everything, so it might just provice the attributes with handle + UUID and fetch things like CEP if available, but perhaps it is possible to have a cache just for the UUIDs registered but that doesn't eliminate the size problem some services can have multiple instances.

@Vudentz - Look how it is done in the discovery manager I have mentioned above. We cache only the parameters of one service detected. Then you are allowed to continue and process next service.

I am not sure now if should I continue with CEP implementation if there is going to be new API - did you already schedule some timing when you wish to implement it?

> @Vudentz Are you saying then that we should have a way to read CEP using `bt_gatt_discovery_params` or not?

That would be a different discovery type that would incorporate reading CEP.

> The size optimization of the params is not really a blocker for this feature request. Do you suggest to do it in that order anyway, and do you intend to both yourself?

I guess it makes sense to do in that order so we don't end up having to reworking the discovery once we introduce a general discovery type.

> Leaving caching of the discovered attributes and values up to the application is perfectly fine. Don't need to have that in the host, the use-case decides what needs to be stored.

It would be perfectly fine if only the application would use the cache but the stack might actually be interested in services as well, for instaces things like GATT, GAP, and other services that the stack itself may have client for. Also for things like CEP it makes sense that the stack has helpers to read it since otherwise applications may have to duplicating code for doing it on their own.
